title: The peaceful life (Kern ch. 13)
hookLine: four ways to teach calmly; the jewel in the king's topknot
tomorrow: From the cracks of the earth (Kern ch. 14)

cards: What's the calmest way to say the thing you think matters most? Picture teaching something you love to people who insult you for it. Do you shout back?
Win the argument? In chapter thirteen, Manjushri asks the Buddha exactly that: in the hard age to come, how should a bodhisattva teach this sutra? The answer isn't a strategy for winning.
It's a way of living so steady that the teaching can be heard through it. Kern's English calls the chapter the peaceful life. And at the end, there's a king with one jewel he holds back.

teach.b: First, the question. Manjushri asks how a bodhisattva can teach the sutra at peace when times are bad, and the Buddha answers with four things to keep.

teach.h: A CALM BODY, A KIND TONGUE.
teach.b: Second, body and tongue. Be patient and gentle, not rash, not easily rattled. Don't chase the powerful to win favor.

Keep a quiet place to sit and see things as empty, without clinging. When you speak, don't dwell on the faults of other people, other teachers or other texts, and don't name people to praise them or tear them down.
Answer kindly and plainly, in a way that fits the person asking. Third, the mind.

teach.h: NO ENVY, NO QUARREL, NO CONTEMPT.
teach.b: No envy, flattery or deceit. Don't sneer at people still learning, and don't pick quarrels. Feel compassion for everyone.
See the Buddhas as fathers and the bodhisattvas as teachers. And keep one wish alive: that people who haven't heard this teaching will someday be brought to it. Fourth, the jewel.
A great king wins a war and rewards his soldiers: fields, villages, towns, clothes, gold, jewels, elephants, horses.

teach.h: THE JEWEL HE KEPT IN HIS HAIR.
teach.b: But one thing he won't hand out, the jewel in the knot of his hair. Giving it lightly would astonish people. He keeps it for the one soldier whose deed is beyond all the rest.
This sutra, the Buddha says, is that jewel. For a long time he gave other teachings; only now does he take this one out.
So the peaceful life is how you carry the jewel: gently, without a fight, without belittling anyone, because what you carry is that precious.

how: In Mahayana communities that read the Lotus Sutra, this chapter's guidance on teaching gently, without quarreling or speaking ill of others, is studied as a model for how to share the teaching.

o: a rest day when no teaching is given at all
teaching gently, without quarrels or belittling anyone
leaving the world to live alone in the forest

games.q: the jewel in the topknot: tap the pairs.
p: asks how to teach in bad times
no envy, no flattery, no quarrels

s: the chapter tells teachers to expose the faults of other teachers
it says the opposite: don't dwell on the faults of other people, teachers or texts.
the king gives his topknot jewel to every brave soldier
fields, gold and horses go to many. the jewel waits for one deed beyond all the rest.
the Buddha compares this sutra to the jewel kept for last
he gave other teachings for a long time, and only now brings this one out.

games.q: you're the king. you've handed out fields, gold and horses. now one soldier stands before you whose deed is beyond all the rest. what do you give?
o: the jewel from the knot of your hair.
nothing more: the rewards are done.
games.why: the king saves the topknot jewel for exactly this. the Buddha says the Lotus is that jewel, kept back and now given.

practice: Think of one thing you'll need to explain to someone soon, a chore to a kid, a change to a coworker, a feeling to a partner, and say it to them in your mind, slowly.
Take out any blame and any edge you'd add to win, until only the thing itself is left, plain and kind. Say it once more, softer, then rest with the breath.

wordCard.voice: The peaceful life. In chapter thirteen, four ways to teach calmly, and a king who keeps one jewel in his hair for the deed beyond all others. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the crest jewel, worn in the knot of hair on the crown.

carryVoice: Your line: the jewel in the topknot. Kept back for the deed beyond all others. Rest well.
